task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hallowed. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hallowed should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: To the divers, the old wreck is hallowed water — no souvenirs, no shouting, no hands on the rail.
Respected earns a nod, and it is far milder than hallowed — nobody whispers around a respected parking rule.
Cherished is loved and protected, but hallowed is stronger still — cherished things are held close; hallowed things are approached quietly.

Sacred means formally set apart as holy — the word a faith itself would use for its altars, relics, and rites. Hallowed climbs to the same height by a slower road: a thing becomes hallowed because generations treat it with reverence. A chapel is sacred by consecration; a battlefield grows hallowed by remembrance.

Holy means belonging to the divine — gods, scripture, heaven's own things. Hallowed is holiness conferred by reverence: bared heads and lowered voices can make a courtroom hallowed with no religion in sight. Holy points at heaven; hallowed points at how people behave.
